title: Sprintless rollout grid & LLM cost sentinel — scratchpad (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working scratchpad for a lightweight, continuous ("sprintless") rollout grid designed for LLM features that must balance latency SLAs, per-token cost, and quality regressions. Focus: hybrid inference (hosted + dedicated + quantized fallbacks).

Context / problem statement:
- We already have multiwave canary playbooks but they assume discrete sprint windows and manual choreography. For many inference changes (model tweaks, routing policy updates, batcher/quantization tuning) we want a lower-friction continuous runway with explicit cost-sensitive gates.
- Observed pain points: repeated partial rollbacks due to cost spikes; slow human-driven rollouts for small quality fixes; unclear ownership when cross-team (product, infra, SRE, ML) touch a single rollout.

Key ideas (top-level):
1) Sprintless grid: small continuous exposures (0.1% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20%) with automatic progressive increments based on signal pass/fail rather than calendar cadence. Hold windows configurable per-signal.
2) Cost sentinel: automated gating on unit economics (avg cost-per-response, tokens-per-request, GPU-hours burn rate) to automatically pause or shrink exposure. Cost gates are first-class as safety signals, not afterthoughts.
3) Hybrid fallback choreography: when quality or latency regressions hit, route to pre-authorized fallback variants (quantized model, older model version, lower-context-mode) with no human step for the first-level fallback.
4) Cross-functional runbook in a single page: roles + signals + automated actions + escalation path. Make it readable for non-engineering stakeholders.

Roles & responsibility (proposal):
- Owner: the team that shipped the change (usually eng-ml or product-hosted-api). Responsible for hypothesis and alert thresholds.
- Steward: product-console rep (oncall rotation) — owns activation, dashboards, and comms.
- On-call SRE: escalation for infra degradation and capacity actions.
- Cost ops (finance/infra): triage when cost sentinel triggers.
- QA/Applied ML: runs focused regressions and supplies quality thresholds / golden prompt sets.

Signals (priority order):
- Latency p90/p99 (route-level and model-level) — hard gate if p99 > target + buffer.
- Quality regressions: automatic evaluation against golden prompt set (delta in BLEU/ROUGE/semantic similarity / model-specific eval metric).
- Cost sentinel: moving avg cost-per-response (tokens * unit price) and 3-day burn acceleration.
- Failure/errors: HTTP 5xx, timeouts, OOMs, decoder hang patterns.
- User visible regression: customer support tags, user NPS dips (manual input).

Example thresholds (starter):
- Hold at 0.1% for min 2 hours and 5000 requests. Proceed if:
  - p99 latency delta < +20% vs baseline AND
  - quality metric delta within tolerance (e.g., semantic-similarity drop < 1.5 pts) AND
  - cost-per-response not > 25% above baseline for 30m window.
- Auto-increment cadence: 0.1% -> 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 25% with exponentially longer hold at higher exposures.

Automated actions (on gate fail):
- Quality fail: auto-fallback to approved model variant (e.g., quant-8bit-v2) for that cohort, notify owner + steward.
- Latency fail: shift traffic to regional fallback pool or dedicated pool; if latency persists beyond 10 minutes, reduce exposure by 50%.
- Cost sentinel trigger: immediately limit traffic to baseline tier (fallback to cheaper model variant) and open triage slack channel; notify cost ops.
- Escalation: only if automated steps do not restore signals within defined windows (e.g., 15m/60m) then wake SRE oncall.

Traffic allocation patterns (grid matrix):
- Grid axes: Exposure % x Fallback mode (none / quantized / older-model / reduced-context).
- Each cell defines: duration, min-requests, signals to evaluate, priority fallback.
- Default starts: 0.1%/none (2h), 0.5%/quantized (3h), 2%/quantized (6h), 10%/older-model (12h) — flexible per-feature.

Observability & dashboards (must-have):
- Per-exposure card: exposure id, model version(s), cohort definition, live traffic %, start time.
- Signal strip: p50/p90/p99 latency, E2E request time, avg tokens, cost-per-response, error-rate, eval-quality-delta for golden set.
- Historical diff: compare current rollout curves to past similar rollouts (helps detect oscillation patterns).
- Cost Sentinel UI: burn rate trend, projected monthly delta if trend persists, hot links to billing.

Comms templates (quick):
- Activation note (to #rollouts): short description, owner, exposure id, initial % and hold policy, expected regressions.
- Auto-fallback alert: link to exposure id, signal that triggered, fallback mode, action taken.
- Rollback summary: root cause if available + mitigation steps + follow-up tasks (bug/PR links).

Playbook snippets (ops automation pseudocode):
- on exposure_start: create exposure_id, provision dashboard, post activation note, start evaluation job against golden set each 5m.
- loop every 5m: fetch signals, evaluate gates; if all_pass -> advance exposure if holds satisfied; if any_fail -> run fallback(action_for_signal).
- fallback(action): route cohort to fallback model(s), mark exposure state "frozen" and set auto-recovery timer (15m).

Example scenario: heavy-cost spike with minor quality regression
1) New model deployed; exposure at 0.5%. Quality delta 0.8 pts (within tolerance), cost-per-response +45% (triggers cost sentinel).
2) Automated action: route 100% of cohort traffic to quantized-v1 until cost stabilizes. Post automated alert.
3) Owner/ML investigates: find decoding change increased tokenization for certain prompts; patch in PR to reduce stop-token verbosity.
4) Re-run small synthetic workload; once cost drops below threshold, unfreeze exposure and resume grid.

Open questions / design tradeoffs (notes to self):
- How conservative should cost sentinel be? We risk false positives for short-lived spikes (e.g., synthetic load). Need smoothing and minimum sample windows.
- Fallback matrix explosion: we need a simple, limited set of fallback recipes per product line to avoid combinatorial complexity.
- Ownership in multi-tenant rollouts: who pays for the cost burns during experimental windows? finance policy needed.
- Interaction with Dedicated pools and Private deployments — fallbacks may require infra provisioning; ensure pre-warmed capacity or pre-approved fallback capacity.

Immediate next steps (practical):
- Prototype: small orchestrator script that runs the 0.1% -> 0.5% -> 2% cadence for a feature flag and emits synthetic evaluation. (Assigned: Miguel)
- Dashboard mock: product-console to mock exposure cards (Assigned: Jin)
- Cost sentinel telemetry: identify billing streams & quick estimator metric (Assigned: Asha)
- Create a small 'fallback cookbook' with 3 approved fallback recipes per product line.

Notes to self / friction logs (fragmentary):
- Keep human-in-loop only for final full rollout (>=50%).
- Need a canonical labeling for exposures to trace across logs/traces/alerts. Use exposure-{team}-{short-feature}-{timestamp}.
- Add a "snooze" mechanism for noisy signals to avoid oscillation.

References / links:
- CON-1427 (rollout grid hypothesis)
- JIRA-RI-893 (cost sentinel spike incident)
- rollout-sim PR 67 (sim harness for progressive exposure)

End of scratchpad — will refine into a playable runbook once prototype behavior is validated.

-- Riley
(last edited 2025-03-18)
